title: Private min pack: add PrometheusRule bundle for SLO burn + critical availability alerts (with promtool validation)
author: Sergio Costa
description: Summary: This PR introduces the initial PrometheusRule bundle for the Private Observability Minimum Pack. It focuses on (a) SLO burn-rate alerting for core request paths and (b) a small set of high-signal critical availability alerts that should page even when SLO math is not yet trustworthy (e.g., missing metrics). It also adds CI validation using promtool to prevent rule load regressions (motivated by SUP-2431 / staging drill where rules silently failed after an upgrade). Scope: In: Burn-rate alerts for API availability + latency and a minimal set of critical availability checks; promtool rule validation wired into CI; docs inline in rule annotations (runbook links as placeholders for now). Out: Full resource exhaustion alerts (GPU/CPU/mem/disk) and pipeline-health rules (coming in follow-ups); per-tenant SLOs (explicitly avoided to reduce cardinality and paging noise). Design notes: - Targets Private deployments (VPC/on-prem). Rules are namespaced and designed to work with kube-prometheus-stack PrometheusRule CRDs. - Burn rate alerts use the standard two-window approach: fast (5m/1h) and slow (30m/6h) windows. - SLOs are defined over aggregated traffic (no tenant label), with optional routing labels included only where they are already bounded (route/model are opt-in in dashboards; SLO rules aggregate them away). - Critical availability alerts include: (1) "no data" / missing metrics for key SLI series, (2) sustained 5xx spikes above a hard threshold, (3) gateway up/down checks. Files/structure: - rules/private-min-pack/slo-burn.prometheusrule.yaml: SLO burn-rate rules (multi-group: api-availability, api-latency). - rules/private-min-pack/critical-availability.prometheusrule.yaml: hard-threshold and missing-signal alerts intended for paging. - scripts/promtool_validate.sh: helper that runs promtool check rules against the bundle. - .github/workflows/ci.yml: new job `prometheus-rules` to run promtool on PRs and main. Example alert (snippet): - alert: RedwoodPrivateAPISLOAvailabilityBurnRateFast expr: (1 - (sum(rate(redwood_gateway_requests_total{status=~"2..|3.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_gateway_requests_total[5m])))) > (14.4 * (1 - 0.999)) for: 2m labels: severity: page service: gateway annotations: summary: "API availability SLO fast burn (gateway)" description: "Fast burn-rate over 5m/1h windows indicates rapid SLO consumption." runbook_url: "https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/x/PRIVATE-OBS-RUNBOOK" Notes on thresholds: Defaults assume 99.9% availability SLO and 99% latency SLO (p95). These are intentionally conservative and can be tuned downstream via value overrides once we have more staging load data. CI: Uses promtool from the official Prometheus container image pinned by digest; validates both syntax and semantic rule parsing. This should catch common indentation and `expr`/`labels` schema issues before merge. Testing: - `promtool check rules rules/private-min-pack/*.yaml` - Loaded into staging kube-prometheus-stack; confirmed rule groups show up in Prometheus UI and fire appropriately under induced 5xx + synthetic traffic. - Verified alerts include stable labels only (cluster/namespace/service/component/severity) to keep dedupe consistent across installs. Follow-ups: - Add pipeline-health + missing-signal alerts for logs/collector (PR #323). - Add resource exhaustion alerts (GPU/CPU/memory/disk) and queue buildup (separate PR). - Replace placeholder runbook links once Confluence pages are published (ENG-2848).

c3e1b2f rules: add latency burn alerts and critical availability group
8b2f0c4 ci: add promtool validation job (pinned image digest)
2e7c9d1 chore: align alert labels/annotations with Private standards
bb0aa62 fix: correct missing `expr` and YAML indentation caught by promtool
review_thread: Sean Gallagher (SRE): "Like the direction. Two asks before approval: (1) ensure we’re not paging on latency burn by default for tiny clusters (need a minimum traffic guard), and (2) add a 'no data' condition for the SLI series so we don’t silently miss outages." Sergio Costa (author): "Ack. Added `min_rps` gating using `sum(rate(...)) > 0.5` (configurable via recording rule later) and added `absent()`-based critical alert for missing SLI metrics." Allison Grant (Observability standards): "Please align label keys with the Private minimum signals standard: use `service` and `component` consistently; avoid `app` label. Also remove route/model from alert labels to keep cardinality down." Sergio Costa: "Updated labels to `service=gateway|runtime`, `component=api`, and aggregated away route/model. Kept route/model only in annotations as an example query." Nadia Rahman (Metrics semantics): "The availability expr uses 2xx/3xx as success; do we want to treat 429 as success for Private installs? Some customers rate-limit at the gateway." Sean Gallagher: "Let’s keep 429 as 'error' for SLO. If customer policy intentionally uses 429, they can adjust SLO or exclude 429 locally." Sergio Costa: "Left 429 as error; added note in the rule comment and README for tuning." Bruno Silva (Installer/packaging): "CI pinning looks good. Please ensure the rules work when installed as a single ConfigMap/CRD file; avoid relying on relative paths." Sergio Costa: "All rule files are self-contained. CI validates each YAML independently and as a glob." Final: Sean approved after rerun; Allison approved with label alignment; Nadia approved after README note.
release_notes: Private min pack now ships baseline SLO burn-rate + critical availability PrometheusRule bundles, with promtool validation in CI to prevent rule load regressions.
